Title: [LSJ] SHambling Hordes strike vs Theft of vitae

Messages.Author: Wolflord
Messages.Body:
Hey guys,

I would like to get confirmation on a ruling Joscha had to make
yesterday (not to doubt you Joscha,; just to lake sure for future
reference)

Shambling Hordes is in Combat with a Random vamp with Thaumaturgy

Say SH is at 4 life.
SH strikes
Thaumaturgy vamp strikes with superior Theft of Vitae
Due to the resolution/timing of Theft, does the Shambling Hordes still
strike for 4, or do you first deduct the theftedlives from the strike.

IE: if vamp thefts for 2 on a SH of 4 life, does the SH strike for 4
or for 2?

ruling yesterday was that you first resolve the theft, so that the
shambling would strike for 2.

thanks for clarifying
/jo

Messages.Author: J
Messages.Body:
> ruling yesterday was that you first resolve the theft, so that the
> shambling would strike for 2.

IANSLJ but, thefts do not resolve before normal strikes. Both strikes
resolve simultaneously - so Theft for 2, Hands for 4.

The thing that confuses people is that stolen blood is applied to the
thefting vamp before damage is applied.

from the rulebook 6.4.5
Steal Blood. This effect moves blood counters (or life counters) from
the target to the striking minion. This does not count as damage, so
the effect cannot be prevented with damage prevention effects. This
effect occurs before the "heal damage" step of damage resolution, so
the stolen blood can be used to heal damage even if the damage is
inflicted simultaneously. If the stolen blood causes the striking
vampire to have more blood than his capacity, the excess drains off
immediately (as usual).

The heal damage step occurs after strikes have resolved - this is when
blood is burned from vampires to heal the damage they take and prevent
themselves from being wounded.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:


The strike is "strength damage" resolving simultaneously with "steal 2 blood".

So 4 damage is applied at the same time 2 blood is moved. Then the damage (4
damage) is resolved.
